provenance.quote: Shall Article 1 of the City of Cherry Hills Village Home Rule Charter, entitled "General Provisions," be amended to add a new Section 1.6 entitled "Home Rule Authority to Regulate the Use of Land", as set forth below? 1.6. Home Rule Authority to Regulate the Use of Land. The authority to plan for, zone, and regulate density, the uses of land, the location and character of structures, and the development of real property within the City are matters of local and municipal concern vested in the City by the Colorado Constitution and this Charter, and such matters shall be regulated only in accordance with this Charter and ordinances enacted pursuant to this Charter. The City shall not be required to adopt or implement laws, standards, approval processes, assessments, plans, or reports on such matters other than as may be enacted by the City Council pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Charter or the voters of the City pursuant to Section 13.11 of this Charter, irrespective of state mandates to do so.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raise Centennial’s sales and use tax by 1 percentage point, to a total city rate of 3.5%, beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $27 million annually initially and amounts based on collections later. Exemptions include groceries for home consumption, gasoline, prescription drugs and other items excluded by city code. Money would fund public works such as traffic safety, street and pothole repairs, roads and aging infrastructure, bridges, sidewalks and pedestrian access. Revenue and spending would appear in the annual independent audit online and receive audit-committee and council review. Revenue and investment earnings could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales and use tax increase, spending reviews and revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Grant Xcel Energy a utility franchise in Glendale from January 1, 2028 through December 31, 2048. It would authorize utility service and the acquisition, construction, installation, operation, maintenance and extension of facilities reasonably needed to provide and distribute service within and through the city.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the utility franchise for the dates and purposes stated.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this proposed franchise.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add a Cherry Hills Village charter provision declaring land-use planning, zoning, density, structures and development to be local municipal matters governed by the city charter and local ordinances. The proposed language states that the city would not be required to adopt state-mandated land-use laws, standards, approval processes, assessments, plans or reports unless enacted by the city council or voters under the charter.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Add the proposed local land-use authority provision to the charter.
measureRecords.noMeans: Leave the charter unchanged under this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add 0.5 percentage points to Sheridan’s sales and use tax beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $986,935 annually initially and amounts based on collections afterward. Revenue would fund public safety, including police, emergency response, equipment and related operations. It could be spent outside otherwise applicable revenue limits. The measure would not restrict collection or spending of the city’s other revenue.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales and use tax increase for public safety and the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Littleton Public Schools property taxes by $10,289,724 in tax year 2026 for collection in 2027. Later amounts could rise to the district’s statutory limit, but year-to-year increases in the property-tax levy after 2026 could not exceed 1 mill. Revenue would go into the general fund for education, including teachers, school safety, academic programs and career readiness, along with purposes voters previously approved. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be collected and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional education taxes within the statutory and annual levy limits, and the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Hills at Cherry Creek Metropolitan District property taxes by $105,000 for collection in 2027, with annual increases afterward equal to inflation plus local growth as defined by Colorado’s constitution. The levy would be set to raise those amounts; the ballot estimates an additional 3.688 mills initially, or about $20.90 per month for a home worth $1 million in 2027. Money would fund district operations, maintenance and other expenses, including walls, parks, playgrounds, courts, recreation space, landscaping and contingencies for infrastructure repairs. Revenue could be collected in addition to other district funds and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits, the statutory 5.5% property-tax limit and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the property-tax increase, annual inflation-and-growth adjustments and revenue-limit exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exceptions.
